title: Wafer Fab Equipment Model
gist: A SemiAnalysis product page describing its Wafer Fab Equipment model: a bottoms-up forecast to 2027 deriving equipment sales from wafer capacity and layer-by-layer node requirements, covering 1.4nm-class logic, high-NA EUV, GAA and backside power delivery, tool-level lithography units and ASPs, and revenue splits by end-use including China. Despite a URL promising NAND WFE analysis, the text is coverage and methodology description for a separate institutional offering, with no forecast numbers disclosed.

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis forecasts semiconductor equipment sales bottoms-up, deriving equipment demand from wafer capacity and process-node requirements modeled as a detailed layer-by-layer flow for advanced logic rather than from top-down capex assumptions.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: A layer-count-driven model is the only way to anticipate WFE mix shifts before chipmakers guide capex.
insights.quote: Our wafer fab model forecasts semiconductor equipment sales through a bottoms-up approach, where wafer capacity and process node requirements drive equipment sales.

insights.claim: The node database extends to 1.4nm-class processes and high-NA EUV, with layer-by-layer lithography requirements covering finFET, GAA and backside power delivery from first EUV use through 1.4nm-equivalent.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: GAA and backside power delivery change layer counts per node - the swing factor for litho and deposition tool demand.
insights.locator: Critical specifications for leading edge and next generation logic

insights.claim: Lithography forecasts are broken out by tool model, units and revenue per chipmaker and process node, backed by a tool database carrying throughput, uptime, rework rate, release date and ASP including upcoming next-generation tools.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Unit-and-ASP level litho visibility is what lets you check ASML shipment guidance against fab-level demand.
insights.locator: Detailed lithography tool database including model, throughput

insights.claim: Equipment sales forecasts through 2027 span lithography, deposition, etch, wafer track and metrology/inspection across Applied Materials, ASML, Lam Research, KLA, Screen, ASMI, Kokusai Electric and Tokyo Electron.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Segment-level splits let you map any WFE datapoint onto the specific vendor P&L it lands in.

insights.claim: Equipment revenue is segmented by end-use into leading edge logic, specialty (trailing edge logic, analog, power, RF), DRAM, NAND/non-volatile and China, treating China as a demand pool distinct from any technology node.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Isolating China as its own end-use bucket is how you strip export-driven distortion out of headline WFE growth.
insights.locator: Sales revenue broken down by end-use segment

insights.claim: Memory coverage on the capacity side is limited to leading-edge 10-nm class DRAM chipmakers, with the whole dataset provided on an annual basis for 2021 to 2027.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Capacity granularity is thinner in memory than in logic - a gap to fill elsewhere when trading memory WFE.
insights.locator: Wafer capacity forecasts through 2027 for advanced logic and leading-edge memory

themes.theme: EUV intensity risk and research business model

insights.claim: The model explicitly forecasts how pattern shaping (Applied Materials' Sculpta tool) and directed self-assembly affect EUV lithography requirements, treating EUV layer demand as contestable rather than a one-way ratchet.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Pattern shaping and DSA are the bear case on EUV layer growth - a direct risk to ASML unit demand assumptions.
insights.quote: Includes forecast on effect of pattern shaping (Applied Material’s Sculpta tool) and directed-self assembly on EUV lithography requirements.
insights.locator: Includes forecast on effect of pattern shaping

insights.claim: SemiAnalysis sells these institutional models separately from newsletter membership, bundling a year of quarterly updates, an onboarding call and ad-hoc analyst calls - a consulting-style tier layered on top of the subscription business.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: The deepest supply-chain data sits behind an institutional tier, so newsletter-only readers are structurally behind.
insights.quote: These models are not included with the annual membership to the SemiAnalysis Newsletter. All models are separate institutional offerings.
insights.locator: The model includes one year of quarterly updates

insights.claim: The captured page is a product description of the wafer fab equipment model itself rather than the NAND WFE analysis its URL slug advertises, so it carries methodology and coverage detail but no forecast numbers or investment thesis.
insights.speaker: SemiAnalysis
insights.so_what: Treat this record as a coverage map of what SemiAnalysis tracks, not as a research call.
